questions.topic: Thin cylinder stresses and volume change
questions.skill: Stresses and dimension changes in thin cylinder
questions.md: A thin cylindrical shell is 4 m long and 1 m in internal diameter. It is subjected to an internal pressure of 1.4 MPa. If the thickness of the sheet is 14 mm, determine the circumferential stress, longitudinal stress, and the changes in diameter, length and volume. Take $E = 200$ GPa and $\mu = 0.3$.

questions.topic: Thin cylinder stresses and volume change
questions.skill: Stresses and dimension changes in thin cylinder
questions.md: A cylindrical shell 3 m long, closed at the ends, has an internal diameter of 1.5 m and a wall thickness of 20 mm. Determine the circumferential and longitudinal stresses induced, and the changes in the dimensions of the shell, if it is subjected to an internal pressure of 1.5 N/mm². Take $E = 2\times10^5\ \text{N/mm}^2$ and Poisson's ratio = 0.3.

questions.topic: Thin cylinder stresses and volume change
questions.skill: Stresses and dimension changes in thin cylinder

If it is subjected to an internal pressure of 90 m of water, calculate the hoop stress, longitudinal stress, and the changes in diameter, length and volume. Take $E = 150$ GPa and $\mu = 0.28$.

questions.topic: Elastic constants and volume change
questions.skill: Elastic constants and volume change of rod
questions.md: A circular rod of 30 mm diameter and 550 mm length is subjected to a tensile force of 70 kN. Determine the modulus of rigidity, bulk modulus and change in volume if Poisson's ratio = 0.3 and Young's modulus $E = 2\times10^5\ \text{N/mm}^2$.

questions.topic: Elastic constants and volume change

questions.md: A bar of 25 mm diameter is tested in tension. It is observed that when a load of 60 kN is applied, the extension measured over a gauge length of 200 mm is 0.12 mm and the contraction in diameter is 0.0045 mm. Determine Poisson's ratio and the elastic constants $E$, $G$ and $K$.

questions.topic: Thermal stress in bar between rigid walls
questions.skill: Thermal stress in series bar between supports

A rod is composed of three segments, as shown in the figure, fixed between two walls. Compute the stress induced in each material by a temperature drop of 30 °C if

(a) the walls are rigid, and
(b) both the supports yield by 0.3 mm.

Take $E_s = 200$ GPa, $E_b = 83$ GPa, $E_a = 70$ GPa, $\alpha_s = 11.7\times10^{-6}/^\circ\text{C}$, $\alpha_b = 18.9\times10^{-6}/^\circ\text{C}$, $\alpha_a = 23\times10^{-6}/^\circ\text{C}$.

| | Bronze | Aluminium | Steel |
|---|---|---|---|
| Length (mm) | 800 | 500 | 400 |
| $A$ (mm²) | 2400 | 1200 | 600 |

questions.topic: Thermal stress in bar between rigid walls

A load of 20 kN is applied (towards the brass end) at the junction at 20 °C. Determine the stresses in the materials when the temperature rises to 50 °C. Take $E_c = 120$ GPa, $\alpha_c = 18\times10^{-6}/^\circ\text{C}$, $E_b = 90$ GPa and $\alpha_b = 20\times10^{-6}/^\circ\text{C}$.

questions.topic: Thermal stress in bar between rigid walls

| Material | Length (mm) | Area (mm²) | $E$ (GPa) | $\alpha$ (/°C) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Steel | 150 | 300 | 200 | $12\times10^{-6}$ |
| Brass | 200 | 400 | 100 | $19\times10^{-6}$ |
| Aluminium | 250 | 500 | 70 | $23\times10^{-6}$ |

Determine the thermal stress developed in each material, assuming the supports are rigid.

questions.topic: Load sharing in composite bars
questions.skill: Load sharing in parallel composite bar
questions.md:
A steel rod of 30 mm diameter is enclosed centrally in a hollow copper tube of external diameter 50 mm and internal diameter 40 mm. The composite bar is then subjected to an axial pull of 45 kN. If the length of each bar is 150 mm, determine:

i. the stresses in the rod and tube, and
ii. the load carried by each bar.

Take $E$ for steel $= 2.1\times10^5\ \text{N/mm}^2$ and for copper $= 1.1\times10^5\ \text{N/mm}^2$.

Take $E$ for copper $= 1.3\times10^5\ \text{N/mm}^2$, for zinc $= 1.0\times10^5\ \text{N/mm}^2$ and for aluminium $= 0.8\times10^5\ \text{N/mm}^2$.

*Figure: the three bars hang side by side between a top support and a rigid bottom plate carrying P = 250 kN.*
